# P32.10a — Single clock authority for publication-disposition `decided_at`

**Requirement ids:** SIG-TRUST-006 (defect repair inside the ADR-124
`publication-eligibility/1` family — no new requirement id, no ADR amendment) ·
**Base:** `devin/p32-10-resolution-evaluator-and-confidence-gates` (stacked on PR #165 — merge this after #165) ·
**Run:** `implement-spec spec=docs/tickets/170a_P32.10a__disposition-single-clock-authority.md live_verification=false` ·
**PR:** #166 · **Ticket:** `docs/tickets/170a_P32.10a__disposition-single-clock-authority.md` (manifest row 170a / "170.5" inserted 2026-09-27)

## What this does

Eliminates the second clock. `decided_at` had two authorities: Python stamped it
host-side (`datetime.now(UTC)`) on every normal write, while the shared
eligibility fragments filter `d.decided_at <= clock_timestamp()` on the
**server** clock. Under Docker Desktop VM clock lag a just-recorded disposition
was transiently future-dated and invisible to the effective-disposition
selector — the 4 intermittent reds P32.10's suite caught in
`tests/db/test_publication_dispositions.py`.

### The fix

- **`policy/eligibility.py`**: `DispositionRecord.decided_at` →
  `datetime | None` (`None` = un-stamped — the database stamps it at INSERT).
  `new_disposition` no longer calls `datetime.now(UTC)`; an explicit
  `decided_at` is accepted only as a documented replay/migration input for
  already-recorded history. `latest_disposition` never selects an un-stamped
  record (SQL-twin parity — `decided_at <= clock_timestamp()` can never see an
  unstamped or future-dated row).
- **`db/dispositions.py`**: `record_disposition` omits `decided_at` from the
  INSERT when the record carries none — `DEFAULT clock_timestamp()` applies
  (the `run_completion` idiom); an explicit value is inserted verbatim for
  replay. `effective_dispositions` now applies the same
  `decided_at <= COALESCE(%s::timestamptz, clock_timestamp())` bound the SQL
  twin carries — a future-dated replay row is recorded history
  (`dispositions_for` shows it) but never the current effective disposition on
  either carrier.
- **sqitch `disposition_decided_at_authority`** (additive — the column already
  carried the default; the writer never let it apply): re-asserts
  `DEFAULT clock_timestamp()` + `COMMENT ON COLUMN` records the contract;
  revert restores the documented prior state; verify asserts both. Existing
  committed values untouched — append-only, no rewrite.

## Regression coverage (all fail on the pre-fix path)

| test | what it proves |
|---|---|
| `test_host_clock_skew_cannot_hide_a_recorded_disposition` | host clock faked +1h (monkeypatch) — record→select still sees the disposition because the DB stamps it; deterministic pre-fix fail |
| `test_normal_write_carries_no_host_stamp` | the INSERT statement omits `decided_at` entirely for normal writes; an explicit replay value carries it (capture-stub conn) |
| `test_future_dated_replay_is_not_the_effective_disposition` | future-dated replay stays in history but is excluded from `effective_dispositions` and the pure `latest_disposition` twin |
| `test_recorded_disposition_is_immediately_visible` | record → immediately-select under the real PG18 container |
| `test_decided_at_default_is_the_database_clock` | the DB default is present and stamps (schema contract pin) |

**Pre-fix proof:** staged against the original writer path —
`3 failed, 20 passed`; the failures are exactly the skew/stamp/parity tests.

## Sweep

Every other writer of a server-clock-compared column already omits it or uses
the DB clock (`run_completion._INSERT`'s `COALESCE(%s, clock_timestamp())`,
`claim_sink`, review/rights/resolution `decided_at`, `ingest_run.started_at`,
`claim_evidence.bound_at`, camera-site tables, `claim.sys_period`).
Read-side as-of `belief` pins (ADR-123) are a different semantic and are
inclusive under the observed skew direction — recorded, not a defect.

**Deferred finding** (different defect class + surface): whole-plan
`sqitch verify` divides by zero — `verify/shared_temporal_contract.sql` pins
`spine_watermark count(*) = 27`, stale since P32.5 added the 28th facet.
Invisible to `make check`/`make test-db` (deploy-only); opened **D-P32.10a-1**
(kind V, cites BL-058) — the repair shape is a maintainer decision (editing a
landed change's verify script under append-only sqitch discipline). This
change's own verify ran directly: `VERIFY-OK`; deploy→revert→deploy green on
real PG18.
